newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent trades higher, excited by Iraqi news.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent trades higher, excited by Iraqi news.

text.p: SIMEX Brent futures traded higher late Monday with the market excited by news that anti-Baghdad Kurdish rebels have regained two more towns from its pro-Baghdad rivals, brokers sauid.
"The news from Iraq as well as technical factors are helping to support the market," one broker said.
November last traded at $24.25 per barrel, up 27 cents from its last IPE close on Friday at $23.98. Brokers said the resistant level for November is $24.50.

The November contract will expire on Wednesday and focus is shifting to the December which was untraded and quoted at $23.73/$23.87. Brokers see resistant for December at $23.76 whith support at $23.30 and the psychological support level at at $23.00.

Rebels from the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) on Sunday retook Sulaimaniya, Iraqi Kurdistan's biggest city from the KUrdistan Democratic Party and had now recaptured Degala and Koi Sanjag after taking control over the strategic Dokan Dam area.
